_about: Stuck-escape ROUTE-ROTATION contract, shared by both runtimes. Every case is
runs it through the JS functions between ESC_CONTRACT_BEGIN/END in
test_escape_route_gate.cpp runs it through escape_route_gate.h. This file is
the only place the expected behaviour is written down, so 'the simulator tests
what the robot does' is checked rather than asserted.
Candidates are PLANAR (z = 0) polylines: the C++ gate measures arc length in 2D
and the JS side in 3D, and those two only agree when z is constant. Real
production paths arrive from the 2D planner already flat; the simulator's
z-varying candidates are hashed by its own 3D code on both of its sides.
expect.pick_index is an index into `candidates`, or the string "none" when the
episode must install nothing. `action` is the terrainGate verdict.
expect.sig_<i> is not used: signatures are pinned in the `signatures` block.
If you change a rule in one implementation and not the other, add the case here
and both probes will disagree with it - that is the whole point.

signatures.name: same centre line, more waypoints -> same signature
5 m route hashes differently from 6 m

cases.name: round 0 installs the route that clearly beats the stuck one
cases.why: 0.30 beats 0.20 by more than install_gain_m; 0.22 does not, so only one candidate is admissible. Ordinary corridor: the trigger dwell is the plain one.

cases.name: round 0 refuses a marginal gain
cases.why: Churning the route for 2 cm is how the escape used to thrash; the first attempt needs a real gain.

cases.name: rescue: a route inside the body budget is replaced below the gain threshold
cases.why: curD < rescue_clearance_m and the candidate reaches it: the dog is wedged, so any route that frees the body wins.

cases.name: round 1 rotates past the signature it already installed
cases.why: Equal clearance in the same rank band, so length orders S6 first - but S6 is what just re-blocked, so the retry takes LONG. This is the livelock fix.

cases.name: round 1 accepts an equal-safety peer, round 0 would not
cases.why: 0.26 is within install_gain_m BELOW curD: after a failed pick the proxy has earned less trust, so a different route of comparable safety gets its turn.

cases.name: exploration never installs a route narrower than the body
cases.why: 0.16 < min_candidate_clearance_m (HALF_W): the relaxed gate is bounded, diversity may not buy a stuck-into-the-wall.

cases.name: terrain penalty rejects a candidate outright, not just to the back of the queue
cases.why: The safest route on paper re-enters the flight the episode is committed to (rule 3), so it is not a candidate at all - and the survivor would have been ranked second anyway.

cases.name: all-identical signatures: the retry falls back rather than pretending
cases.why: Two waypoint spacings of one line share a signature, so no candidate is new; past round 0 the episode re-uses the rotated pick and says so via fallback=true.

cases.name: rule 1: mid-flight, no route swap
cases.why: Re-planning from a tread the recogniser has no support model for is how the escape used to send the dog off the flight.

cases.name: rule 2: mid-flight plus a required reversal aims at the landing
cases.why: The retreat target is the nearest portal cell, not "back along the path".

cases.name: a landing is standable floor, so rotation runs there
cases.why: onStairNow is true up to and including the last row beside the portal; only the snap radius separates "committed" from "standing on a platform".

cases.name: stair_commit_enable off restores the terrain-blind escape
cases.why: The opt-out has to be total, or a robot without stair detection cannot escape on a staircase at all.

cases.name: escape_only_at_landing off allows a mid-flight swap
cases.why: Terrain awareness stays on (reversals still aim at the landing); only the no-swap rule is relaxed.

cases.name: rule 4: a floor transition waits out the longer dwell
cases.why: A slow gait handover is not a block; escapeDwellMs must answer with transition_dwell_ms.

cases.name: max_rounds saturates the attempt index
cases.why: escRound / escapeRound clamp, so a long stuck spell stops widening its ambition instead of running away with it.
